title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LA0LE_0RA0RF_1RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LA0LE_0RA0RF_1RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the trip rule and the seven rules that end an epoch in the common cases, for every size (lean/Rules.lean). Followed with these rules, the run from blank tape has not halted in 1039,417 steps: 37,692 epochs, all but one of which are instances of the proved rules. Whether it ever halts depends on the residues modulo 3 of numbers that grow by about 10/3 per epoch, a Collatz-like question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 87,950 cells have been visited and 52,346 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The trip and the start
claims.text: 1^3 (01)^(m+1) C> at the right end (blank to the right) becomes (01)^(m+6) C> in 6m + 45 steps, whatever lies further left; by induction, 1^(3k) (01)^(m+1) C> becomes (01)^(m+1+5k) C> in k(6m + 30) + 15k² steps. From blank tape the machine reaches (01)^9 C> in 89 steps.

claims.title: The epoch ends, in the common cases
claims.text: With level 1 = 1^r (01)^M, r = 0 or 2: zero_blank, zero_dec, zero_merge (r = 0: level 1 becomes 1^(2M+6) (01)^3 or 1^(2M+7) (01)^3, taking a 01 or the ones of level 2), two_blank, two_trip, two_dec, two_merge (r = 2: level 2 takes one step and level 1 becomes 1^(2M-4) (01)^3 or 1^(2M-8) (01)^3). Each holds for every M, the sizes of the other levels and the rest of the tape, with the exact step count. Not covered: a carry from level 2 into level 3, and level-2 runs of 01 shorter than 4.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>39,417</sup> steps
claims.text: py/stack.py keeps the tape as its list of levels, does the trips of an epoch at once and ends each epoch with the proved rules (when none applies, by plain simulation with level 1 cut down to 30, 31 and 32 copies, extrapolated linearly). In two minutes it runs 37,692 epochs and reaches 1039,417 steps; 37,691 epoch ends are instances of the Lean rules, one is a carry into level 3. The first 9 epochs (3·1010 steps) agree with the plain C simulator in step count and tape (py/stack.py check 9).

claims.title: The rule at every level
claims.text: A level k ≥ 2 changes only when the level below it ends an epoch with two ones left. It then takes one step: a trip, 1^(n+3) (01)^m to 1^n (01)^(m+7); or, with no ones, a rebuild to 1^(2m+5) (01)^6 (or 1^(2m+4+p) (01)^6), taking from level k+1; or, with two ones, a carry into level k+1 and a rebuild to 1^(2m-6) (01)^6 after a trip there, 1^(2m-10) (01)^6 otherwise. A level reduced to a single one is the same tape as one more 01 on the level above (a pop). Observed in every simulated case with m ≥ 5; smaller m behaves differently and is not tabulated.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when state F reads a 1; no proved rule does that, and plain simulation of all 8,064 event configurations with up to two small extra levels found no halt. A proof of non-halting would need rules for every case (the carries and small levels too) closing over all stacks that can arise; the order in which the cases come is set by sizes modulo 3.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LA0LE_0RA0RF_1RC---/py/stack.py check 8      # the stack simulator against the plain one
python3 holdouts/1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RE_1LA0LE_0RA0RF_1RC---/py/stack.py run 120      # one line per epoch, for two minutes

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a stack of counters on its tape. It works on the top one with a simple proved rule, and each time that counter runs out it rebuilds it about 10/3 times larger, either borrowing from the next counter or making the next counter take a step, depending on the counter's size modulo 3. Followed exactly with the proved rules, it has not halted in 10<sup>39,417</sup> steps.

facts.text: No halt, following the Lean-proved rules epoch by epoch.
Steps of one trip, proved for every m.
The trip and the common epoch ends, proved for all sizes.
Growth of level 1 per epoch (steps × about 11).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.525).
After 109 steps the tape spans 87,950 cells (15 left of the start, 69,265 right), with a density of 1s of 0.595.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: A stack of levels
html: Every time the head is at the right end of the tape in state C, the tape left of it reads as a stack of levels, each a run of ones followed by a run of 01, separated by single zeros:

Level 1 is the one next to the head. It is huge; the levels above it are small and change rarely. A level never has exactly one 1: 0 1 (01)^m is just (01)^(m+1) on the level above.

sections.heading: Trips: three ones become five 01
html: From 1^(n+3) (01)^(m+1) C> the head runs left to the ones, turns three of them into 01 pairs, runs back and adds two more at the right end: 1^n (01)^(m+6) C>, in 6m + 45 steps. Lean proves this for every m and every tape further left (trip), and k trips in a row by induction (trips). So level 1 = 1^n (01)^m becomes, after n/3 trips, 1^r (01)^(m + 5n/3) with r = n mod 3.

sections.heading: Rebuilding level 1, by n mod 3
html: With M copies of 01 left and r ones:

• r = 0. The head rebuilds level 1 as 1^(2M+7) (01)^3, taking the last 01 of level 2; if level 2 has no 01 it joins instead: 1^(2M+6+n2) (01)^3 (zero_dec, zero_merge, zero_blank).
  • r = 1. Nothing happens: 0 1 (01)^M is level 2 with M + 1 more copies of 01. Level 1 is popped and level 2 carries on with its ones (by trips, now at the right end).
  • r = 2. Level 2 takes one step and level 1 becomes 1^(2M-4) (01)^3 after a trip of level 2, 1^(2M-8) (01)^3 otherwise. A level-2 step is a trip 1^(n+3) (01)^q → 1^n (01)^(q+7), or, with no ones, a rebuild to 1^(2q+5) (01)^6 that takes from level 3; on blank tape a new level 1^4 (01)^6 is pushed (two_trip, two_dec, two_merge, two_blank).

All of these are proved in Lean for every size. Each epoch multiplies level 1 by about 10/3 (M is about 5n/3 and the new n is about 2M), so the step count grows about elevenfold per epoch. The first epochs:

sections.heading: Every level is the same counter, run slower
html: A level k ≥ 2 moves only when the level below it ends an epoch with two ones left, and then it takes one step of the same kind: a trip (adding 7 copies of 01 instead of 5), a rebuild to 1^(2m+5) (01)^6 when it has no ones, or, when it has two ones, a carry: level k+1 takes a step and level k is rebuilt to 1^(2m-6) (01)^6 or 1^(2m-10) (01)^6. A level left with one 1 pops into the level above. This is a multi-level counter in which each digit is itself a counter of the same kind.

In practice the stack stays shallow: level 1 is popped whenever its size is 1 mod 3, which takes level 2 with it. In 37,692 epochs from blank tape a carry into level 3 happened once, at epoch 30,402 (level 2 = 1^2 (01)^72, rebuilt as 1^134 (01)^6 with a new level 3 1^4 (01)^6).

sections.heading: Not in any proved rule
html: The machine halts when state F reads a 1. None of the proved rules does, so a halt would have to come from a case they do not cover: a carry, or a level whose run of 01 is very short. Simulating every event with level 1 large and up to two small levels above it (8,064 cases) found no halt. Whether the run ever reaches a bad case depends on the sizes of level 1 modulo 3, epoch after epoch, which nobody knows how to predict.

sections.heading: Proved, computed, observed
html: Lean, kernel: the halting configurations; no halt in 10,000 steps; the start (start, 89 steps), the trip and k trips, and the seven epoch-end rules (lean/Rules.lean). Lean, native_decide: no halt in 107 steps.

Computed (trusted): following the proved rules from blank tape, no halt in 1039,417 steps (py/stack.py, checked against the plain simulator for the first 3·1010 steps). Observed: the rule at levels 3 and up, and the 10/3 growth.

summary: The tape is a stack of levels 1^n (01)^m. The head works on level 1: each trip turns three ones into five copies of 01, and when fewer than three ones are left the level is rebuilt about 10/3 times larger, either taking a 01 from level 2, or making level 2 take one trip of its own (a carry). Which happens is set by the size of level 1 modulo 3.
